newsitem.title: USA: IBM hits 52-week high, nears all-time high.
newsitem.headline: IBM hits 52-week high, nears all-time high.

text.p: Shares of International Business Machines Corp reached a 52-week high and neared an all-time historical high of 175-7/8, as investors viewed the computer giant as an increasingly safe technology investment.

IBM also scored a major publicity coup this weekend, after its Deep Blue supercomputer made chess history, as it defeated the world chess champion Garry Kasparov on Sunday, but traders and analysts said this was not a factor in the stock's climb.
"IBM is viewed today as a relatively safe investment," said Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial analyst. "It's a good place to put money." IBM shares were up 4-1/2 to 172.
"Everybody is pouring money into it," said one technology trader. "It's a big cap name that is acting well, as opposed to a big cap name that isn't acting well, like Intel Corp."

A two-for-one stock split was recently approved by its shareholders, which was effective May 9. IBM's shares, trading on a when-issued basis, were up 3-5/8 to 86-1/8. The new shares will be distributed to shareholders on May 27.
